content: 1. Short-acting antacids and pazopanib: Short-acting antacids may be used as alternatives to proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) and H2 receptor antagonists when co-administered with pazopanib. However, pazopanib and antacids should be administered several hours apart to avoid interactions. Calcium carbonate and magnesium hydroxide can reduce the plasma levels and efficacy of pazopanib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration of pazopanib with drugs that elevate gastric pH. If antacids are necessary, separate their administration from pazopanib by several hours. 2. Calcium carbonate and penbutolol: Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of penbutolol by reducing its gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer calcium carbonate and penbutolol at least 2 hours apart. Monitor closely for reduced therapeutic effects of penbutolol. 3. Magnesium hydroxide and penicillamine: Magnesium hydroxide reduces the absorption and efficacy of penicillamine by interfering with gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer magnesium hydroxide and penicillamine at least 2 hours apart. Monitor closely for reduced therapeutic effects of penicillamine. 4. Calcium carbonate and perindopril: Calcium carbonate may reduce the effects of perindopril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely for reduced efficacy of perindopril. 5. Calcium carbonate and pexidartinib: Calcium carbonate decreases the plasma levels and efficacy of pexidartinib by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy as needed and monitor closely for reduced therapeutic effects of pexidartinib. 6. Famotidine and pexidartinib: Famotidine increases the plasma levels and effects of pexidartinib by altering gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, administer pexidartinib 2 hours before or 10 hours after taking an H2 receptor antagonist. 7. Calcium carbonate and quinapril: Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of quinapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely for reduced efficacy of quinapril. 8. Calcium carbonate and quinidine: Calcium carbonate increases the plasma levels of quinidine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urinary environment. Elevated quinidine levels may lead to cardiac conduction disturbances and arrhythmias. Use caution and monitor closely for signs of toxicity. 9. Magnesium hydroxide and raltegravir: Magnesium hydroxide reduces the plasma levels and efficacy of raltegravir by binding to it in the gastrointestinal tract. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, administer raltegravir at least 6 hours apart from magnesium-containing antacids. 10. Calcium carbonate and rifampin: Calcium carbonate reduces the absorption and efficacy of rifampin. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before taking antacids to avoid this interaction. Monitor closely for reduced therapeutic effects of rifampin. 11. Famotidine and rilpivirine: Famotidine decreases the plasma levels and efficacy of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy as needed and monitor closely for treatment failure or the development of resistance to rilpivirine or NNRTIs. If antacids must be used, administer them at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. 12. Calcium carbonate and rosuvastatin: Calcium carbonate reduces the plasma levels and efficacy of rosuvastatin by inhibiting its gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Administer calcium carbonate and rosuvastatin at least 2 hours apart. Monitor closely for reduced therapeutic effects of rosuvastatin. 13. Magnesium hydroxide and sotrasib: Magnesium hydroxide reduces the plasma levels and efficacy of sotrasib by inhibiting its gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, administer sotrasib 4 hours before or 10 hours after taking magnesium hydroxide. 14. Famotidine and sotrasib: Famotidine decreases the plasma levels and efficacy of sotrasib by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 15. Calcium carbonate and sotrasib: Calcium carbonate reduces the plasma levels and efficacy of sotrasib by inhibiting its gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug.
